For GOOGL fiscal year 2022 (the annual flow covering 2022-01-01 through 2022-12-31, per the data reported in the 2024 disclosure year), the three income-statement measures are, in reported USD units: revenue of $282,836,000,000; operating income of $74,842,000,000; and net income of $59,972,000,000. These are distinct measures and should not be conflated. Revenue is the top-line total of sales recognized over the fiscal year, before any costs or expenses are deducted. Operating income is what remains after operating costs and expenses are subtracted from revenue, so it measures profitability of core operations and excludes non-operating items. Net income is the bottom line after all items, including non-operating and tax effects, and is the amount attributable to the period's earnings. The gap between revenue and operating income reflects operating cost intensity, and the gap between operating income and net income reflects non-operating and tax effects. All three figures share the same annual period, so they are internally consistent and directly comparable within fiscal 2022.

For GOOGL fiscal 2024 (period 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31), the reported income-statement measures are: revenue of USD 350,018,000,000; operating income of USD 112,390,000,000; and net income of USD 100,118,000,000. These three measures are distinct layers of the income statement and are not interchangeable. Revenue is the top line: total amounts recognized from sales of products and services (Search/YouTube advertising, Google Cloud, subscriptions and devices, etc.), before any costs or expenses are deducted. Operating income is revenue less cost of revenues and operating expenses (R&D, sales and marketing, general and administrative); it excludes non-operating items such as other income/expense and income taxes, so it measures profitability of core operations. Net income is the bottom line: the residual after all expenses, non-operating items and the provision for income taxes are applied, and it is the earnings attributable to the period that flow into shareholders' equity. Accordingly, operating income (USD 112.390 billion) exceeds net income (USD 100.118 billion) by USD 12.272 billion, reflecting the net effect of non-operating items and taxes, while both are well below revenue because operating costs and cost of revenues are substantial. All three values are annual flow figures in USD for the same January-to-December 2024 fiscal period, so they are directly comparable within that period. Note that the revenue observation carries report_year 2024 while the operating income and net income observations carry report_year 2025; the underlying fiscal period is identical across all three (2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31), so the difference reflects disclosure/filing year rather than a period mismatch. No growth rates or prior-year comparisons were requested and none are provided; no report was generated.
